clue.text: Problem jazz fan picks up in gossip

indicators.note: picking something up means holding it, so the jazz fan's letters go around the problem

parts.note: a cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast
a hitch is a snag or problem

explanation.surface: A jazz fan overhears some trouble while chatting idly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jazz fan' is old slang for a hip devotee; 'picks up' signals one piece holding the other, and 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: idle, light conversation about trivial matters is gossip.

clue.text: Renegade caught by Henry makes a bloomer

indicators.note: being caught by someone means being held inside them, so the renegade sits within Henry

parts.note: Hal is the familiar form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
a renegade is a rebel

explanation.surface: A deserter arrested by a man called Henry commits a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a British word for a blunder; here it is a flower, something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a bluebell-like wildflower is a plant that blooms, hence a bloomer.

clue.text: Italian Trot, a revolutionary dictator?

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests overturning, so these letters are turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: An Italian Trotskyist revolutionary may turn into a tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ITALIAN TROT A; 'Trot' is short for Trotskyist, adding to the political picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an autocrat holding absolute power runs an authoritarian one-party state; the question mark marks the loose noun use.

clue.text: Travel at speed damaged outside of limousine

parts.note: hurt means harmed or damaged

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A limousine is damaged on its exterior while speeding.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to rush or career along at great speed.

clue.text: Mexican food cheers company

parts.note: ta and cheers are both British informal thanks

explanation.surface: A Mexican snack lifts the spirits of the group.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a folded tortilla with a filling is a staple Mexican dish.

clue.text: Composer with uplifting part for one unaccompanied

parts.note: J S Bach, the German composer

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting up means the word reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a role is an actor's part

explanation.surface: A composer writes an inspiring piece for a soloist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' reverses ROLE to ELOR; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an unmarried man goes through life without a wife beside him.

clue.text: TV cook endlessly found in food shop

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter of the cook's name is dropped

parts.note: Delia Smith is a famous British television cook

explanation.surface: A television chef is always to be found in a grocer's.
explanation.walkthrough: DELIA Smith is a well-known British TV cook; 'endlessly' drops her final A. 'found in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbreviation of delicatessen, a shop selling prepared foods.

clue.text: What one may do during cheese course or entree?

definitions.text: What one may do during cheese course
definitions.meaning: at a formal dinner the fortified wine is handed round the table with the cheese
entree in its sense of right of entry or access

explanation.surface: A dinner-party question about cheese and the main course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entree' poses as a dish; it means admission. The first reading splits into PASS PORT, a British dinner custom.
explanation.definitionFit: A travel document grants a holder admission to foreign countries, i.e. entry.

clue.text: Four articles about medium's curse

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the articles go round the medium

parts.note: an, a, the and a are four articles of English grammar
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: Four newspaper pieces discuss a spiritualist's curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medium' suggests a psychic but gives M; ''s' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a formal ecclesiastical ban or a thing that is utterly detested is a curse.

clue.text: Worry about appearing in business paper

indicators.note: something appearing in a paper sits inside it, so these letters go within the newspaper

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times, a British business newspaper
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious about a story in the financial press.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to be anxious and fidget over something.

clue.text: Working with stars, fool collects prize (that's right)

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so the fool's letters enclose the rest

parts.note: an ass is a fool
a trophy is a prize
sic, Latin for thus, is printed to say a quoted word is right as written

explanation.surface: A fool working with celebrities walks off with an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collects' signals enclosure; 'that's right' is the editor's Latin marker for a quotation printed as found. 'with stars' suggests celebrities but means the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the branch of science studying the physics of stars and space, i.e. work concerned with heavenly bodies.

clue.text: Theatre worker, a star that's upcoming caught by surprise

indicators.note: being caught by something means sitting inside it

parts.note: to stagger someone is to surprise them

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a big name is a star

explanation.surface: A rising theatre star is taken aback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upcoming' reverses the two pieces to EMANA, and 'caught by' places them inside the verb for surprise; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the person who runs the backstage side of a theatre production.

clue.text: Engineer gets best clothes for chemical plant

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army corps
finery is one's smartest clothing

explanation.surface: An engineer dresses up smartly for a visit to a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an industrial plant that purifies crude oil or sugar.

clue.text: Canadian singer-songwriter, no longer this?

definitions.meaning: someone who has aged is no longer youthful

explanation.surface: A veteran Canadian musician is getting on.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a joke on the singer, now in his eighties.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil is the musician's forename; the adjective means youthful, which an elderly person no longer is.

clue.text: Shed small amount of light on tea that's stewed

indicators.note: a small amount of a word is its opening letter
stewed tea has been left to brew too long, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone throws a little light on a pot of overbrewed tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a verb with 'light'; it is the noun. 'that's stewed' rearranges ON TEA to EANTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a simple outbuilding with a sloping roof propped against a wall.

clue.text: Simple plant found in several gardens

indicators.note: found in means the letters lie within these words

explanation.surface: A basic plant grows in a number of gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: seaweeds and pond scum are simple non-flowering water plants.

clue.text: Single-handedly captures international gangster

indicators.note: capturing means holding within, so the first word's letters surround the second

parts.note: doing something single-handedly is doing it alone
a cap is a sporting international, a player chosen for the national side

explanation.surface: A lone hero seizes a criminal from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: In British sport an 'international' is a player capped for the national side, the cap being the award itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the notorious Chicago mobster of the Prohibition era.

clue.text: Group popular in the Nineties touring East being less happy

indicators.note: a band touring an area goes round it, so the band's letters surround the other piece

parts.note: Blur was a leading Britpop band of the 1990s
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A 1990s band on tour in the east gets downhearted.
explanation.walkthrough: Blur were a British band of the Britpop era; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: feeling blue means feeling sad, so this comparative is sadder.

clue.text: Someone scary ravaged money bag

indicators.note: something ravaged is wrecked, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A frightening figure plundered a bag of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the imaginary monster used to frighten children.

clue.text: Give out ecstasy in front of Cambridge college

indicators.note: placed in front of means coming first in the answer

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, is in Cambridge, Massachusetts

explanation.surface: Drugs are handed out outside a university college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cambridge' suggests England, but this is Cambridge, Massachusetts.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to discharge or send forth, as light or a sound.

clue.text: Person hard to satisfy that is boxing former boxer

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the Latin phrase surrounds the boxer

parts.note: id est is Latin for that is
Muhammad Ali, the late heavyweight champion

explanation.surface: A demanding person keeps an old prizefighter in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' looks like the sport but means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: someone holding to perfect standards is rarely pleased by reality.

clue.text: Reconnoitring with a view to breaking cover

definitions.text: Reconnoitring with a view to breaking
definitions.meaning: to case a joint is criminal slang for scouting a place before a break-in
an outer covering or shell, as on a sausage or a cartridge

explanation.surface: Scouting the area before breaking cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking cover' reads as one phrase; split it after 'breaking', meaning breaking in.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang verb for scouting premises, and the noun for a protective outer shell.

clue.text: Achieve success through Republican Party ties

parts.note: the GOP, Grand Old Party, is the US Republican Party
laces tie shoes

explanation.surface: Someone gets on in life through links with the Republicans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'through' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone who will be successful in their career is said to be headed far.

clue.text: Colour in a kind of statistical chart a small digit

indicators.note: in means placed inside the chart's letters

parts.note: a pie chart shows proportions as slices
ink colours a page

explanation.surface: Someone shades a pie chart's slice and adds a tiny figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colour' looks like it gives PINK; it is INK. 'digit' suggests a number but means a finger.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the little finger is the smallest digit of the hand.

clue.text: Planes in navy crashed somewhere in USA

indicators.note: crashed means wrecked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Naval aircraft have crashed somewhere in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Keystone State is one of the fifty states of America.

clue.text: Pond creature wife caught in appropriate item

indicators.note: being caught in a net means sitting inside it

parts.note: to net is to take or appropriate, read here as the catch of an item

explanation.surface: A wife is snared in something she meant to take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught in' puts W inside NET, which means appropriate; 'item' seems to round out the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small amphibian that lives in ponds.

clue.text: Division of Novotel

indicators.note: of means taken out of this hotel name, whose letters contain the answer

explanation.surface: A section of a hotel chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Division' reads as a part of a company; in Parliament it is a vote.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword-friendly sense: in Parliament a division is a formal ballot, members dividing into lobbies.

clue.text: Good message to departed stagehand

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is written on gravestones

explanation.surface: A kind farewell note to a theatre worker who has left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'departed' suggests someone leaving a job; it means the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a technician moving scenery or film equipment is called this.

clue.text: Report of events from all directions found

parts.note: N, E, W and S are the four compass points
to found metal is to cast it in a mould

explanation.surface: A report has been gathered from all over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' is not the past of find but the verb meaning to mould metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a radio or television bulletin reporting the day's events.

clue.text: Strongly criticise directors' salary?

parts.note: exec, short for executive, is a company director
rate is the rate of pay

explanation.surface: A question of whether to attack bosses' pay.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as EXEC RATE, an executive's pay rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to denounce or loathe something vehemently.
